name: Translate Website & Rank Globally with SEO & GEO – MultiLipi AI Translation
author: KUNAL SINGH SHEKHAWAT

sections.description:
MultiLipi Translate fetches permitted languages from the MultiLipi backend, keeps the API key on the WordPress server, and renders target-language public pages with translated HTML before they are sent to visitors or crawlers.

Features include language subdirectories, routing for standard WordPress URLs and public custom post types, WooCommerce product/store URL compatibility, hreflang output, an SEO Pack with manual target-language metadata fields and an optional multilingual sitemap, server-rendered text and social metadata translation, an automatic floating language switcher plus shortcode, conditional language-content shortcodes, API-managed language storage and redirects, a central local slug-translation editor, indexed target-language WordPress search with optional on-demand and visitor-driven modes, server response caching, API-enabled language-subdirectory llms.txt plus public-page .md files using the existing saved MultiLipi API key, and API-enabled best-effort LLM request analytics.

External Services

This plugin connects to MultiLipi over HTTPS after a site administrator configures a MultiLipi account API key. The saved key remains on the WordPress server. Browser translation requests use the site’s local WordPress REST API.

Service: MultiLipi API at https://multilipiseo.multilipi.com/
Used for: Fetching language and feature configuration and saved slug mappings; translating eligible page text and URL slugs; synchronizing slug mappings; reporting translation page usage; and reverse-translating search phrases when on-demand search is enabled and authorized by the API.
Data sent: The API key, site domain and URL path, source and target languages, text selected for translation, and source/translated slug paths. Search phrases are sent only for the enabled on-demand search fallback. Configuration and slug synchronization run on administrator requests, settings refreshes, or local slug updates; page translation runs on eligible target-language requests and configured background work.

Optional LLM files: When enabled by the verified API configuration, https://multilipiseo-2.multilipi.com/ receives the server-side API key, domain, language, URL path and eligible public-page HTML to generate llms.txt and Markdown content.

LLM request analytics: When the verified API configuration enables LLM or schema capabilities, https://multilipiseo.multilipi.com/domain/api/llm-analytics/ receives anonymous public-request events containing domain/path, detected AI crawler category, language, response status, response time and User-Agent. These events do not include the API key, cookies, IP address, query string, request body or page content.

Terms: https://multilipi.com/terms_and_conditions
Privacy Policy: https://multilipi.com/privacy_policy

Bundled libraries

Flag icons use flag-icons 6.6.6 by Panayiotis Lipiridis (MIT license). The CSS and SVGs are served locally from this plugin. The license is included at assets/vendor/flag-icons/LICENSE.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install its ZIP in WordPress.
  2. Activate MultiLipi Translate.
  3. Open MultiLipi > Settings, enter an API key, and fetch language settings.
  4. Enable target languages and save.
sections.changelog:
3.0.0

  • Retain the multilipi-multilingual-seo folder and entry filename for in-place upgrades from v2, using WordPress.org updates in this release.
  • Automatically preserve the saved API key, source/target languages, selected languages, and API feature flags without reactivation.
  • Refresh newer API configuration fields in a bounded background job; preserve local configuration if the service is unavailable.
  • Preserve multilingual sitemap discovery and redirect old admin and sitemap entry points.
  • Leave v2 slug mappings untouched and do not import them into v3.
  • Import saved MultiLipi slug dictionaries when fetching configuration, with manual override precedence and collision checks.
  • Hide the 404 translation and background pretranslation controls while preserving saved preferences.

0.7.6

  • Simplify settings to the API key, target languages, and five SEO/search options; manage translation, slug, LLM, and usage behavior from fixed policy or API capabilities.
  • Support session language storage for none, persistent cookies for dynamic_translation and language_redirection, and redirects for language_redirection.
  • Restore a saved language on revisited source pages in place when dynamic translation is enabled; manual selections always navigate to language subdirectories.
  • Honor use_dynamic_translation for browser text updates and dynamic content while preserving server rendering and page-view reporting.

0.7.5

  • Move Settings and Slug translations into a top-level MultiLipi admin menu using the original MultiLipi icon.
  • Refresh the settings page with grouped controls, connection and language sections, and responsive styling.
  • Keep settings notices, language-switcher previews, and admin actions working at the new menu location.

0.7.4

  • Repair the production settings-profile rendering path so packaged plugins pass PHP parsing and activate normally.
  • Keep hidden production-profile settings and directory-routing choices intact when administrators save visible settings.

0.7.3

  • Fix plugin deletion when WordPress runs uninstall cleanup without loading the main plugin bootstrap.
  • Cache-bust browser translation assets after updates and recover safely from transient or expired translation-session tokens.
  • Add an explicit per-row Remove control to the Slug translations editor.

0.7.2

  • Make language-switcher button, dropdown, and hover colors consistently use the configured theme tokens across the catalog.
  • Keep automatic floating switchers at their configured position from first render, and correctly mount automatic embedded switchers at their configured target.

0.7.1

  • Build target-language URLs from the canonical source-site URL so a source language other than English cannot produce nested directories such as /en/en-gb/.
  • Save the expanded language-configuration response, including switcher data, URL filter rules, and class-only block exclusions.
  • Exclude matching target routes from translation, generated links, hreflang, sitemap, search, REST, and LLM/Markdown output; choose a 404 or temporary source-URL redirect in Settings.
  • Treat each exlclude_attribute value as a class name only, and invalidate llms.txt cache entries when URL filter rules change.
  • Add per-language directory-routing policies: keep native source routing, let MultiLipi claim the directory, or use native-first hybrid fallback after a confirmed native 404 on WordPress 6.1+. Policies can also be selected manually for custom routes WordPress cannot detect; protected WordPress directories remain source-only.
  • Add a default-on setting to publish or suppress hybrid URLs in hreflang and the MultiLipi XML sitemap without changing their visitor routing.

0.7.0

  • Add an opt-in administrator-only LLM diagnostics panel showing bounded, redacted upstream API request and response excerpts without exposing the saved API key or visitor data.
  • Add a Settings switch to bypass stored llms.txt and Markdown responses. Disabled-cache responses use no-store headers while retaining generation locks and rate limits.
  • Restrict llms.txt discovery to enabled language subdirectories and add target-home Markdown aliases: /hi/.md, /hi.md, and /hi/index.html.md.
  • Resolve translated-slug and index.php Markdown routes back to their source-side path, and remove public no-translation/switcher regions before sending locally rendered HTML to the Markdown service.
  • Add opt-in LLM request analytics for anonymous public WordPress responses when the fetched backend configuration enables is_llms or is_schema.
  • Send the backend-compatible bot-family classification, source domain/path, language, response status, latency, and bounded raw User-Agent to the separate unauthenticated telemetry endpoint; no API key, cookie, IP address, query string, page content, or request body is sent.
  • Deliver telemetry only after PHP-FPM has completed the visitor response, with a bounded single in-flight request and outage cool-off; hosts without a safe after-response primitive skip analytics.
  • Add strict normalization for backend LLM/schema flags, so string values such as no and false do not accidentally enable the feature.

0.6.0

  • Add opt-in server-side language-subdirectory llms.txt and public Markdown routes, including /{language}/llms.txt, /about.md, /hi/.md, /hi.md, and /hi/index.html.md.
  • Use the existing saved MultiLipi API key as the server-side Bearer token for LLM/Markdown generation; no separate LLM key is stored or exposed.
  • Add bounded caching, single-flight generation, rate limits, lifecycle regeneration, and privacy exclusions for generated LLM files.

0.5.11

  • Emit portable query-form child sitemap URLs so nginx hosts that intercept unknown XML files cannot return a server-level 404 before WordPress runs.

0.5.10

  • Prevent SEO-plugin URL hooks from printing duplicate raw canonical/Open Graph URLs into translated page heads.
  • Make multilingual sitemap child URLs work before rewrite rules are refreshed and add the MultiLipi sitemap index to compatible sitemap indexes, including Rank Math.

0.5.9

  • Add an SEO Pack that safely localizes standard canonical, Open Graph/Twitter URL, and semantic page JSON-LD output alongside common SEO plugins.
  • Add manual target-language SEO title, description, Open Graph, and Twitter overrides for public posts, products, custom post types, and terms.
  • Add an off-by-default multilingual XML sitemap with hreflang alternates, advertised alongside existing WordPress/SEO-plugin sitemaps.

0.5.8

  • Decode valid percent-encoded UTF-8 text before writing translated document titles, descriptions, and social metadata, so browser tabs display readable target-language text.

0.5.7

  • Add an off-by-default Visitor-driven search index that translates and stores only a public target-language post/product a visitor actually opens, without queueing cron or bulk-pretranslating the site.

0.5.6

  • Add an off-by-default, backend-authorized and rate-limited on-demand source-language search fallback for target-language queries with no local translated-index match.

0.5.5

  • Server-render initial target-language HTML for explicitly enabled logged-in visitors, with private/no-store response headers to protect personalized pages from shared caches.

0.5.4

  • Show WordPress percent-encoded Unicode localized slugs as readable text in the Slug translations editor while retaining their safe internal URL form.

0.5.3

  • Translate mixed search labels such as “Search results: “हुडी”” while keeping the visitor-entered target-language term out of API requests.
  • Add opt-in Background pretranslation. It is off by default, so pages and automatic slugs are translated on eligible visitor visits rather than queued for cron.

0.5.2

  • Add a nonce-protected Settings action to permanently delete all MultiLipi data for the current site.
  • Delete all plugin-owned settings, caches, queued jobs, slug mappings, and translated-search tables automatically on uninstall, including every site in a multisite network.

0.5.1

  • Keep Gutenberg and other recognized GET search forms inside the active language directory instead of submitting to the source-language home URL.

0.5.0

  • Add conditional language-content shortcodes, including safe migration aliases when no other plugin owns them.
  • Add an opt-in, browser-only language redirect for first visits to the source home page; explicit switcher choices are remembered.
  • Translate existing Open Graph/Twitter title and description fields server-side, translate visible select/button controls, honor common no-translation markers, and translate only genuinely new dynamic element subtrees after a server-rendered page.

0.4.0

  • Fix translated WooCommerce product slugs and generic public custom-post-type routes by replaying WordPress’s viewable CPT query handling after the language directory is removed.
  • Add WooCommerce compatibility for product-search actions, Cart/Checkout/My Account URLs and supported endpoints, same-origin Woo AJAX URLs, return redirects, cart-item links, and safely targeted fragment translation.
  • Add plugin-neutral canonical/Open Graph URL normalization for standard SEO-plugin head output.

0.3.1

  • Add Settings > Slug translations: a searchable, paginated editor for local post/page/CPT and taxonomy-term translated slugs by target language.

0.3.0

  • Add opt-in local automatic slug translation for published posts, public custom post types, and public terms through queued jobs or a safe first eligible, query-free target-language GET visit, while preserving manual slug overrides and collision protection.
  • Add opt-in indexed multilingual WordPress search for translated post titles and content on target-language search pages.

0.2.2

  • Preserve WordPress static front-page routing under a language directory instead of falling back to the configured posts page.

0.2.1

  • Rewrite same-site and root homepage links emitted directly by themes and builders into the active language directory.

0.2.0

  • Render target-language pages with translated HTML before sending the page to visitors.

0.1.2

  • Fix persistence of fetched language configuration after saving or reloading Settings.

0.1.1

  • Show the fetched, key-free backend language configuration directly in Settings.
  • Add an automatic public floating language selector and improve shortcode placement guidance.

0.1.0

  • Initial MultiLipi API integration.
